questions.question: You come to this sign at the end of the street. What does it require of you?
choices: Come to a complete stop, then give the right-of-way to pedestrians and all cross traffic before moving again
Slow down and keep rolling, stopping only if a vehicle is actually coming
This marks the beginning of a no-passing zone
This is advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: The eight-sided shape is reserved for stop signs, and nothing else uses it. The handbook is explicit: you must stop completely, then give the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffic before you move again. A rolling stop is not a stop.
choiceExplanations: Slowing and rolling through is closer to what a YIELD sign asks for; an octagon demands a full stop every single time.
The beginning of a no-passing zone is marked by the pennant — a sideways triangle on the left of the road.
Advance warning of a railroad crossing is given by the round yellow-and-black sign, not by an octagon.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: These eight-sided signs are reserved for stop signs.  These signs mean you must stop completely.

questions.imageAlt: Red eight-sided octagon sign with the white word STOP

questions.question: You reach this sign at an intersection that has no pavement markings and no crosswalk. Where must you stop?
choices: Before entering the intersection, at a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions
With your front wheels already inside the intersection so you can see around parked cars
Level with the sign itself, whatever you can see from there
Anywhere in the block, as long as you stopped once before the corner
questions.explanation: With no markings or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection — and the handbook adds the part drivers forget: stop at a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions. Stopping where you cannot see is a stop that protects nobody.
choiceExplanations: Rolling into the intersection to see better puts your vehicle in the path of cross traffic; stop first, then edge forward only if the view is blocked.
The sign's position is not the rule — the rule is stopping before the intersection at a point where you can see all directions.
One stop somewhere in the block does not satisfy the sign; the stop must be before the intersection itself.

source.sourceQuote: Stop at a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions.

questions.imageAlt: Red eight-sided octagon sign with the white word STOP

questions.question: What does this sign shape require?
choices: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic
Come to a complete stop every time, then proceed
A school zone is ahead or you are at a school crossing
The road ahead is more slippery than other roads when wet
questions.explanation: The upside-down triangle is the yield shape. It requires you to give the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic — you may keep moving if the way is genuinely clear, but the other traffic goes first.
choiceExplanations: A mandatory complete stop every time is the octagon's message; yield asks you to give way, not to stop unconditionally.
School zones are marked by the five-sided pentagon sign, not by an upside-down triangle.
Slippery-when-wet is a yellow diamond warning sign showing a car with wavy skid marks.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

source.sourceQuote: This shape requires that you yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic.

questions.imageAlt: Red and white upside-down triangle sign with the word YIELD

questions.question: You are on a ramp merging onto a busy road and this sign faces you at the end of the ramp. A line of traffic is coming. What do you do?
choices: Let the traffic already on the road go first, and enter only when there is a safe gap
Enter immediately — traffic on the main road must open a gap for you
Stop completely at the sign even if the road is empty, then go
Speed up and force your way into the nearest gap
questions.explanation: This shape requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic. On a ramp that means the traffic already on the road goes first; you fit yourself into a gap rather than making one.
choiceExplanations: The sign puts the duty on you, not on them — yielding means the other traffic keeps its right-of-way.
An unconditional complete stop is what an octagon requires; a yield lets you keep rolling when the way is clear.
Forcing a gap is the opposite of yielding and is exactly the crash this sign exists to prevent.

questions.question: This sideways-triangle sign is posted on the left-hand side of the road. What is it telling you?
choices: A no-passing zone begins here
A slow-moving vehicle is ahead of you
You must yield to traffic entering from the left
There is a school crossing ahead
questions.explanation: The pennant — a long sideways triangle — marks the beginning of a no-passing zone. It is posted on the left so it faces the driver who would be tempted to cross the centre line.
choiceExplanations: A slow-moving vehicle carries an upright triangular emblem with a red border and orange centre, mounted on the vehicle itself.
Yielding is the message of the upside-down triangle, which is red and white and says YIELD.
School zones and school crossings are marked by the five-sided pentagon sign.

questions.question: A no-passing zone is about to begin. Which sign shape carries that message?
choices: The pennant — a long triangle pointing sideways, shown here
The octagon
The pentagon
The circle
questions.explanation: Shape alone tells you a great deal before you can read a word. The pennant shape is used for one thing: marking the beginning of a no-passing zone.
choiceExplanations: The octagon is reserved for stop signs and is never used for anything else.
The pentagon warns of a school zone ahead or marks a school zone crossing.
The round yellow-and-black sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: What does this round yellow sign mean?
choices: Advance warning that a railroad crossing is ahead
A traffic circle or roundabout is ahead
You are entering a no-passing zone
A crosswalk crosses the road ahead
questions.explanation: The circle is the one shape reserved for this job: a yellow-and-black round sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead. It appears well before the tracks so you have time to slow and look.
choiceExplanations: The circular shape here has nothing to do with a roundabout — the handbook assigns the circle to railroad advance warning.
No-passing zones are marked by the pennant, a sideways triangle posted on the left of the road.
A crosswalk ahead is shown by a yellow diamond with a walking figure on it.

questions.question: You are driving a country road and this sign appears at the roadside. What should you expect next?
choices: Tracks crossing the road ahead — slow down, look and listen for a train
A sharp curve that is too sharp for the regular highway speed
A lane ending, so traffic will be moving into your lane
A bridge or underpass with low clearance
questions.explanation: This sign is advance warning, not the crossing itself. It gives you distance in which to slow down, look both ways along the tracks and be ready to stop, because you must yield to all trains.
choiceExplanations: A curve too sharp for highway speed is shown by a yellow diamond with a curving arrow, not by a round sign.
A lane ending is a yellow diamond in which one of two lanes narrows into the other.
Low clearance is a yellow diamond that prints the actual height, such as 12'-6", between two arrows.

questions.question: What does this five-sided sign warn you about?
choices: A school zone ahead, or a school zone crossing
A pedestrian crosswalk on an ordinary street
A playground with no school attached
A no-passing zone beginning
questions.explanation: The five-sided pentagon is the school shape. It warns of a school zone ahead — the school grounds and any street abutting them — or marks a school zone crossing.
choiceExplanations: An ordinary crosswalk warning is a yellow diamond with a single walking figure, not a five-sided sign.
The handbook assigns this shape to school zones and school zone crossings specifically.
The beginning of a no-passing zone is marked by the pennant, a long sideways triangle.

source.sourceQuote: This sign warns of a school zone

questions.imageAlt: Five-sided yellow pentagon sign showing two children walking

questions.question: You pass this sign at 2:45 in the afternoon and children are on the sidewalk. What is the maximum speed limit in this zone?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in a school zone is 15 m.p.h. when children are present or when otherwise specified. It is one of the lowest limits you will ever drive, and it applies to the school grounds and the street for 125 feet along it.
choiceExplanations: 20 m.p.h. is not the figure the handbook gives for a school zone.
25 m.p.h. is a common business and residential limit, but it is too fast for a school zone with children present.
35 m.p.h. is an ordinary street speed and far above the school-zone maximum.

questions.question: You come up behind a vehicle displaying this emblem. What does it identify?
choices: A slow moving vehicle, or a vehicle that has made an emergency stop
A vehicle carrying hazardous materials
A student driver on a road test
A vehicle that has the right-of-way over you
questions.explanation: A right-side-up triangle with a reflective red border and a fluorescent orange centre identifies a slow moving vehicle or a vehicle which has made an emergency stop. Expect to close on it far faster than you think.
choiceExplanations: Hazardous-materials loads are identified by diamond-shaped placards with numbers and symbols, not by this emblem.
Student drivers are not identified by this emblem; it marks the speed of the vehicle, not the experience of the driver.
The emblem confers no right-of-way; it is a warning about speed so that you can slow in time.

questions.question: You are travelling 55 m.p.h. on a two-lane road at dusk and this emblem appears ahead of you. What is the safe reading of it?
choices: The vehicle ahead is moving far slower than you, or has stopped in an emergency — begin slowing now
The vehicle ahead is about to turn left
The vehicle is a wide load and you may not pass it at all
It is a reflector with no particular meaning
questions.explanation: The emblem exists because the speed difference is the danger. At 55 m.p.h. behind a vehicle doing 20, the gap closes in seconds, so the emblem is your cue to slow early rather than brake hard.
choiceExplanations: A left turn is announced by the vehicle's turn signal or an arm straight out, not by this emblem.
The emblem says nothing about width or about passing being prohibited; it identifies a slow moving vehicle.
It is a defined traffic emblem with a specific meaning, not a decorative reflector.

questions.question: This sign is posted over the middle lane of a highway. What is that lane for?
choices: Left turns only, made by traffic from either direction
Passing slower vehicles when the way ahead is clear
Traffic that is turning right at the next intersection
Emergency vehicles only
questions.explanation: This is the dual turn lane sign. The lane under it is used only for making left turns, and traffic from both directions will be using it — which is why you must look before you enter it.
choiceExplanations: Passing in this lane is specifically forbidden: never use a turning lane to overtake and pass other vehicles.
The sign's arrows curve left from both directions; right turns are made from the right-hand lane.
The lane is a shared left-turn lane for ordinary traffic, not a reserved emergency lane.

questions.imageAlt: Tall white sign reading CENTER LANE ONLY with two curved arrows turning left and right

questions.question: The car in front of you is slow, and the lane under this sign is empty. May you use it to get past?
choices: No — never use a turning lane to overtake and pass other vehicles
Yes, as long as you return to your lane within 100 feet
Yes, if no vehicle is waiting to turn left
Yes, but only below 25 m.p.h.
questions.explanation: The handbook states the rule flatly: never use a turning lane to overtake and pass other vehicles. The lane looks empty to you, but traffic from the opposite direction can enter it at any moment to turn.
choiceExplanations: No distance makes it legal — the prohibition on passing in a turning lane has no time or distance exception.
An empty lane is exactly the trap: a driver coming the other way may swing into it to turn at the same moment.
Speed does not change the rule; the lane is for turning, from either direction, only.

questions.question: You are on a ramp at night and your headlights pick up this sign facing you. What has happened?
choices: You are travelling against traffic — traffic in that direction is prohibited, and you are likely to meet a vehicle head on
The road ahead is closed for construction
You are approaching a one-way cross street
You have entered a no-passing zone
questions.explanation: Wrong Way and Do Not Enter both warn that traffic in that direction is prohibited. The handbook puts the consequence plainly: if you choose a lane marked with either of these signs you will likely run into another vehicle. Stop, and get out of that lane.
choiceExplanations: Construction closures are orange work-zone signs or a ROAD CLOSED barricade, not a red WRONG WAY sign.
A one-way cross street is announced by the black-and-white ONE WAY sign with an arrow, which is information, not a prohibition on you.
No-passing zones are marked by the yellow pennant on the left of the road.

source.sourceQuote: These signs warn  you  that  traffic  in  that  direction  is prohibited.

questions.imageAlt: Red rectangular sign with white letters reading WRONG WAY

questions.question: Where would you normally expect to meet the sign shown here?
choices: Facing you if you have entered an exit ramp or a one-way roadway in the wrong direction
On the back of a slow moving farm vehicle
Above a lane that is used for left turns from both directions
At the entrance to a rest area
questions.explanation: These signs face the driver who is already going the wrong way — most often on an exit ramp taken by mistake. Seeing one means the traffic coming toward you has the road and you do not.
choiceExplanations: Slow moving vehicles display an orange-and-red triangular emblem, not a WRONG WAY sign.
A lane shared for left turns from both directions is marked by the CENTER LANE ONLY dual turn lane sign.
Rest areas are marked by white-on-blue motorist services signs.

questions.question: This sign is standing at an opening in the divider of a divided highway. What is it there to do?
choices: Remind you which side of the divider you belong on
Warn you that the road ahead narrows to one lane
Tell you that the cross street is one way
Mark the start of a passing zone
questions.explanation: Lane Directions signs are posted between divided highway lanes and placed at the openings in the dividers where streets intersect the highway. Their whole job is to keep you on the correct side of the divider.
choiceExplanations: A lane ending is a yellow diamond warning sign showing one lane merging into the other, not a black-and-white instruction.
A one-way cross street is announced by the ONE WAY sign with a horizontal arrow.
Passing zones are not marked by this sign; the pennant marks where a no-passing zone begins.

questions.imageAlt: White rectangular sign reading KEEP RIGHT with an arrow pointing up and to the right

questions.question: You are crossing a divided highway and this sign faces you at the gap in the median. What does the symbol instruct you to do?
choices: Pass to the right of the divider shown on the sign
Stop at the divider and wait for a gap
Cross the divider only when no traffic is coming
Turn around, because the road is closed
questions.explanation: The symbol is literal: the arrow passes to the right of the black divider. These signs sit at the openings in the dividers to remind you which side of the divider you belong on.
choiceExplanations: The sign gives you a side of the divider to use; a required stop would be shown by a stop sign or a stop line.
You do not choose a side by whether traffic is coming — the divider has a correct side, and the sign names it.
A closed road is shown by a ROAD CLOSED barricade with orange and white stripes.

questions.question: What does this sign prohibit?
choices: Turning around in the middle of a street or an intersection
Turning left at the intersection
Turning right at the intersection
Entering the street at all
questions.explanation: The U-shaped arrow with a red circle and slash is the No U-Turn sign: it means do not turn around in the middle of a street or an intersection. Everything else — left, right, straight on — is still allowed unless another sign says otherwise.
choiceExplanations: A prohibited left turn is shown by a left-pointing arrow inside the red circle and slash, not a U-shaped arrow.
A prohibited right turn is shown by a right-pointing arrow inside the red circle and slash.
A street you may not enter at all is marked DO NOT ENTER or WRONG WAY in red and white.

questions.question: On this sign and on every sign like it, what does the red circle with the diagonal bar through it always mean?
choices: NO — whatever is pictured inside the circle is prohibited
CAUTION — whatever is pictured inside needs extra care
It marks the sign as a warning of danger ahead
It shows which movement is recommended
questions.explanation: A red outline with a diagonal bar through it always means NO. Learn that one convention and you can read a sign you have never seen before: find the picture inside the circle, and that is the thing you may not do.
choiceExplanations: Caution is carried by yellow diamond warning signs, not by a red circle and bar.
Warnings of danger ahead are yellow diamonds; the red circle and bar is a regulatory prohibition.
The red slash marks the movement that is forbidden, which is the exact opposite of a recommendation.

questions.question: You are in the right-hand lane at an intersection and this sign is posted. What does it tell you?
choices: You may not turn right at this intersection
You may not turn left at this intersection
You may not turn around at this intersection
You may not go straight through this intersection
questions.explanation: The arrow inside the red circle and slash names the movement that is forbidden. Here the arrow turns right, so the right turn is prohibited — these signs are used where you would be meeting a one way street or where turning would be unsafe.
choiceExplanations: A prohibited left turn shows a left-pointing arrow inside the circle; read the direction of the arrow, not the word.
A prohibited U-turn shows a U-shaped arrow doubling back on itself.
The sign prohibits only the movement drawn inside the circle, so going straight on is unaffected.

questions.question: This sign faces you at an intersection. Why is a sign like this usually posted here?
choices: Because the cross street is one way, or because turning that way would be unsafe
Because the intersection has a traffic signal
Because the road ahead is a divided highway
Because a school zone begins at the corner
questions.explanation: No Right Turn and No Left Turn signs indicate which direction you cannot turn at an intersection. The handbook gives the reason: they are used when meeting a one way street, or in situations where it is unsafe to turn.
choiceExplanations: A traffic signal ahead is announced by a yellow diamond showing a signal head, not by a red circle and bar.
A divided highway is not the reason for a turn prohibition; the red slash simply forbids the movement drawn inside it.
School zones are marked by the five-sided pentagon sign, not by a turn prohibition.

questions.question: You are about to turn into a roadway and this sign faces you. What does it mean?
choices: Traffic in that direction is prohibited — do not use that roadway
Enter slowly and yield to traffic already there
The roadway is private property
The roadway is closed only to trucks
questions.explanation: DO NOT ENTER warns that traffic in that direction is prohibited. Like WRONG WAY, it faces the driver who is about to travel against the flow, and the handbook warns that a lane marked this way will likely put you into another vehicle.
choiceExplanations: There is no slow-and-yield version of this sign; the movement is prohibited outright.
The sign is a traffic control device about direction of travel, not a statement about who owns the road.
The sign applies to all traffic, not to one class of vehicle.

questions.question: Most square and rectangular regulatory signs are white with black letters. Why is this one red with white letters instead?
choices: Because the message is very important
Because it is a warning of a hazard ahead rather than a law
Because it applies only at night
Because it is a guide sign giving directions
questions.explanation: Colour is a message of its own. Most regulatory signs are white with black letters; when the message is very important, the sign is red with white letters. Red is the handbook's way of saying this one is not advisory.
choiceExplanations: Hazards ahead are warnings, and warnings are yellow diamonds — red is reserved for the most important regulatory messages.
Nothing about red restricts a sign to night-time; the prohibition applies at all hours.
Guide signs tell you where you are and how to get somewhere, and are usually white on green.

questions.question: You are stopped at a cross street and this sign faces you. What is it telling you?
choices: The cross street carries traffic in one direction only — the direction the arrow points
Your own street becomes one way from here on
You must turn in the direction of the arrow
Passing is prohibited beyond this point
questions.explanation: The ONE WAY sign tells you when a cross street has traffic running in one direction only. The arrow shows which way that traffic runs, so you know which way you may turn into it — and which way would put you head on into it.
choiceExplanations: The sign describes the cross street it is posted on, not the road you are currently travelling.
It does not compel a turn; it tells you which direction the cross street runs if you do turn.
No-passing zones are marked by the yellow pennant sign on the left of the road.

questions.question: You turn into the street marked by this sign, and at the next block you look for another one-way street. What does the handbook say you can usually expect?
choices: The next consecutive block usually runs in the opposite direction
Every consecutive block runs the same way as this one
One-way streets never appear in consecutive blocks
The direction changes with the time of day
questions.explanation: Where there are one-way streets, usually every consecutive block runs in the opposite direction. Knowing the pattern lets you plan a turn one block ahead instead of discovering you cannot make it.
choiceExplanations: If consecutive blocks all ran the same way, traffic would have no route back; the handbook describes them alternating.
One-way streets typically do appear in runs of consecutive blocks — that is the pattern being described.
Direction reversal by time of day is what lane use control signals manage, not ordinary one-way streets.

questions.question: What exactly does the number on this sign represent?
choices: The fastest speed you may drive under optimal weather and road conditions
The speed you should drive whatever the conditions
The recommended safe speed, which you may legally exceed
The minimum speed allowed on this road
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the fastest speed you may drive under optimal weather and road conditions. Ice, fog, rain or heavy traffic do not raise the number, but they do mean the safe speed is lower than it.
choiceExplanations: The posted number is a ceiling for the best conditions, not a target to hold in rain, snow or fog.
A black-on-yellow advisory sign is a recommendation; a black-on-white SPEED LIMIT sign is the law.
Minimum speeds are shown separately when they apply; this number is the maximum.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.imageAlt: White rectangular sign reading SPEED LIMIT 55

questions.question: This sign is posted on a residential street, and heavy rain has made the road slick. What speed does the law allow you?
choices: Up to 25 m.p.h., but the rain means the safe speed is lower than the posted number
Exactly 25 m.p.h., because the posted limit is also the required speed
Up to 35 m.p.h., because the limit is only a guideline
Any speed you judge safe, because posted limits do not apply in rain
questions.explanation: The posted figure is the fastest speed for optimal weather and road conditions. In rain you are still bound by the 25, and the conditions oblige you to drive under it — the number is a ceiling, never a requirement.
choiceExplanations: A limit is a maximum, not a speed you must maintain; conditions often make a lower speed the only safe one.
A black-on-white speed limit is enforceable law, not a guideline, and exceeding it is an offence.
Bad weather never suspends a posted limit; it lowers the speed that is actually safe within it.

questions.question: You are leaving an interstate on an exit ramp and the sign at the ramp is black lettering on a yellow background rather than black on white. What kind of sign is it?
choices: An advisory speed sign showing the maximum recommended safe speed for the ramp
A speed limit sign that has faded from white to yellow
A warning that the ramp is closed
A minimum speed sign for the ramp
questions.explanation: Advisory speed signs are found at interstate entrances and exit ramps, showing the maximum recommended safe speed for driving on the ramp, and they are black on yellow. The black-on-white SPEED LIMIT sign shown here is the enforceable limit for the road itself.
choiceExplanations: The colour difference is deliberate and standardised, not the result of weathering.
A closed ramp would be marked with orange work-zone signs or a barricade, not a yellow speed plate.
Advisory signs give a recommended maximum for the curve of the ramp, not a minimum.

questions.question: What is this yellow diamond warning you about?
choices: This section of highway is more slippery than other roads when wet
The road ahead has loose gravel
A sharp curve is coming up
Two-way traffic begins ahead
questions.explanation: The car with wavy skid marks means this section of highway is more slippery than other roads when wet. The handbook's instruction is short: reduce your speed.
choiceExplanations: The symbol shows a vehicle sliding, and the handbook ties the warning to wet conditions specifically.
A sharp curve is shown by a diamond with a bending arrow, not by a skidding car.
Two-way traffic is shown by a diamond with two straight arrows pointing in opposite directions.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a car with wavy skid lines behind its wheels

questions.question: Rain has just started and you pass this sign at the posted 55 m.p.h. limit. What should you do?
choices: Reduce your speed — this stretch is more slippery than other roads when wet
Hold 55, since the posted limit has not changed
Brake hard now to test how much grip you have
Move to the left lane, where the surface is never slippery
questions.explanation: The sign exists because this stretch loses grip faster than the roads around it. The posted limit still says 55, but the limit assumes optimal conditions; the handbook's response to this sign is to reduce your speed.
choiceExplanations: Holding the posted limit ignores that the limit is set for optimal weather and road conditions.
Hard braking on a surface you already suspect is slick is how a skid starts, not how you test for one.
The warning applies to the section of highway, not to one lane of it.

questions.question: What does this yellow diamond tell you?
choices: You are on a two-way road, so traffic can come toward you
A lane is being added on your side of the road
The lane you are in is ending
Traffic may be merging into your lane from the right
questions.explanation: Two straight arrows pointing in opposite directions are used to indicate that you are on a two-way road. It matters most where a driver might assume the road is one way — coming off a divided section, for instance.
choiceExplanations: An added lane is shown by an arrow joining alongside yours without a conflict, not by opposing arrows.
A lane ending is shown by one of two lanes narrowing into the other.
Merging traffic is shown by a short arrow joining your straight arrow at an angle.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign with two straight black arrows, one pointing up and one pointing down

questions.question: What does this yellow diamond warn you about?
choices: A lane is ending — in this case the right lane
An extra lane is being added on the right
The road ahead is slippery when wet
There is a crosswalk ahead
questions.explanation: The symbol shows the right-hand edge bending in to meet the lane beside it: a lane will be ending, here the right lane. If you are in it, plan a lane change early rather than at the point where the pavement runs out.
choiceExplanations: An added lane opens up room rather than taking it away, and its symbol shows a new arrow joining alongside.
Slippery when wet is shown by a car with wavy skid marks behind it.
A crosswalk ahead is shown by a diamond with a walking figure on it.

source.sourceQuote: To  warn  you  that  a  lane  will be  ending; in this case, the right lane.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing two lane lines, the right-hand one bending in to meet the left

questions.question: If the symbol on this sign were reversed — the bend on the left instead of the right — what would it mean?
choices: The left lane is ending instead of the right
Two lanes are ending at once
A lane is being added on the left
The bend has no meaning; the symbol is always drawn this way
questions.explanation: The handbook says it directly: the symbol would be reversed if the left lane is ending. Read the side the bend is on and you know which lane runs out — which tells you whether it is your problem or the other driver's.
choiceExplanations: The symbol shows one lane merging into another, not both ending.
An added lane is a separate sign showing a new arrow appearing alongside the existing one.
The orientation is the whole message, and it is mirrored deliberately to show which side is ending.

source.sourceQuote: The symbol would be  reversed  if  the  left  lane  is ending.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing two lane lines, the right-hand one bending in to meet the left

questions.question: A plain black cross fills this yellow diamond. What is it warning you about?
choices: Crossroads ahead — watch for other vehicles entering or leaving the highway
A railroad crossing ahead
A four-way stop ahead where every driver must stop
A hospital ahead
questions.explanation: The plain cross symbol warns of crossroads ahead. The instruction that comes with it is the useful part: watch for other vehicles entering or leaving the highway, because they may not have seen you.
choiceExplanations: A railroad crossing is warned of by a round yellow sign with an X and the letters R R, or by a crossbuck at the tracks.
The sign warns of the intersection's existence; it does not itself impose a stop on anyone.
A hospital is shown by a blue motorist services sign with a white H.

questions.question: You are on a rural highway at 55 m.p.h. and this sign appears. What is the specific risk it is naming?
choices: A side road joins from the right, so a vehicle may pull out in front of you or turn off ahead of you
Your own road is about to end at a T-junction
The right lane of your road is closing
A driveway is reserved for farm vehicles
questions.explanation: The stem on the right of the symbol is a side road joining the highway. The handbook's warning for crossroads and side roads is the same: watch for other vehicles entering or leaving the highway.
choiceExplanations: The through road on the symbol continues straight; a road ending at a T would show the stem meeting a crossing bar ahead of you.
A lane closing is shown by two lane lines narrowing into one, not by a joining side road.
The sign is about a road that joins yours, and it does not identify what kind of vehicles use it.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a vertical line with a side road branching off to the right

questions.question: What does this yellow diamond tell you about the road ahead?
choices: A series of curves is coming that is too sharp to take at the regular highway speed
The road ahead is slippery when wet
A lane is about to be added
You are entering a no-passing zone
questions.explanation: The arrow that snakes back and forth warns of curves in the road ahead. The handbook's point about all of these curve signs is the same: the curve is too sharp to take at the regular highway speed, and an advisory speed sign may be attached.
choiceExplanations: Slippery when wet is shown by a car with wavy skid marks beneath it.
An added lane is shown by a second arrow joining alongside the first.
A no-passing zone begins at the yellow pennant sign on the left-hand side of the road.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing an arrow winding left and right as it goes up

questions.question: You meet this sign on a highway where the limit is 55 m.p.h. How fast should you take what is ahead?
choices: Slower than 55 — the turn is too sharp for the regular highway speed, and any advisory sign attached tells you how much slower
55, because the posted limit has not changed
Faster, to keep momentum through the bends
Any speed, as long as you stay in your lane
questions.explanation: Curve and turn warnings exist precisely because the geometry, not the speed limit, decides what is safe. The curve is too sharp to take at the regular highway speed, and an advisory speed sign may be attached to tell you the recommended figure.
choiceExplanations: The posted limit assumes optimal conditions on normal road geometry; a curve sign is telling you this stretch is not that.
Carrying extra speed into a sharp turn is how a vehicle runs wide or leaves the road entirely.
Staying in your lane is precisely what becomes difficult if you enter the turn too fast.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing an arrow that jogs sharply right and then left

questions.question: A small yellow sign reading 30 is bolted underneath this warning sign. What is that number?
choices: An advisory speed — the recommended safe speed for the turn
The legal speed limit for the rest of the road
The distance in feet to the turn
The minimum speed you must maintain through the turn
questions.explanation: Where a curve or sharp turn is too sharp for the regular highway speed, an advisory speed sign may be attached. The plate gives the speed at which the turn can be taken safely, and it is a recommendation — but one built from the actual geometry of the bend.
choiceExplanations: The legal limit for the road is on a separate black-on-white SPEED LIMIT sign; this plate applies to the turn.
Distances on warning signs are spelled out with units, for example 1000 FT, not left as a bare number.
Advisory plates give a maximum recommended speed, never a minimum.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a black arrow turning sharply to the left

questions.question: A short arrow joins the straight arrow on this yellow diamond. What is it warning you about?
choices: Traffic may be moving into your lane
Your lane is ending and you must move over
An extra lane is being added for you
The road ahead has two-way traffic
questions.explanation: The short arrow joining your straight arrow means traffic may be moving into your lane. The handbook's instruction is to be ready to change your speed or your lane to avoid a crash — the merging driver may have very little room.
choiceExplanations: Your lane ending is a different sign, showing two lane lines narrowing into one.
An added lane gives the joining traffic its own lane; this symbol shows it arriving in yours.
Two-way traffic is shown by two straight arrows pointing in opposite directions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Be ready to change your  speed  or  your  lane  to avoid a crash.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a straight arrow with a shorter arrow joining it from the right

questions.question: You pass this sign and a car appears on the ramp beside you, level with your door. What does the handbook tell you to be ready to do?
choices: Change your speed or your lane to avoid a crash
Hold your speed and lane exactly, so the other driver can predict you
Brake hard and let every merging vehicle in
Sound your horn and keep going
questions.explanation: Merging traffic is the one warning that asks you to act rather than just look: be ready to change your speed or your lane to avoid a crash. Adjusting early gives the joining driver somewhere to go.
choiceExplanations: Predictability matters, but this sign specifically asks you to be ready to adjust your speed or lane.
Hard braking on a busy road creates a second hazard behind you; adjusting early is the point.
A horn warns, but it does not create the gap the merging vehicle needs.

source.sourceQuote: Be ready to change your  speed  or  your  lane  to avoid a crash.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a straight arrow with a shorter arrow joining it from the right

questions.question: Before you work out what the symbol on this sign means, what do its yellow colour and diamond shape already tell you?
choices: That it warns of possible danger ahead
That it states a traffic law you must obey
That it tells you where you are and how to get somewhere
That it marks a construction work zone
questions.explanation: Shape and colour do work of their own. A yellow diamond is a warning sign: it warns of possible danger ahead and may carry symbols or written warnings, usually with no explanatory words beneath.
choiceExplanations: Traffic laws are carried by regulatory signs, which are square or rectangular and usually white with black letters.
Where you are and how to get somewhere is the job of guide signs, most of which are white on green.
Work zones use the same diamond shape but in orange; orange is the basic colour for construction devices.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: They warn of possible danger ahead and may have symbols or written warnings.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond warning sign showing two curved black arrows passing on either side of a black median island

questions.question: A curving arrow joins alongside the straight arrow on this yellow diamond, with a dashed line between them. What does that mean?
choices: A lane is being added, so joining traffic will have its own lane
Traffic will be merging into the lane you are in
Your lane is ending ahead
The road divides into a divided highway
questions.explanation: This sign advises you of an added lane. It is the friendly relative of the merging sign: the traffic joining from the side gets a lane of its own, so it does not have to force its way into yours.
choiceExplanations: Merging traffic is the sign where the joining arrow runs into your arrow; here the new lane stays separate.
A lane ending is shown by two lane lines narrowing into one, which is the opposite of this.
The symbol shows a lane being added alongside, not a median separating opposing traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: This sign is to advise you of an added lane.

questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a curving arrow joining alongside a straight arrow, with a dashed line between them

questions.question: Why does it matter whether the sign ahead advises an added lane rather than merging traffic?
choices: With an added lane the joining traffic has its own lane; with merging traffic it is coming into yours
An added lane means you must change lanes; merging traffic means you may stay
An added lane applies only on interstates; merging traffic applies only in towns
There is no practical difference between the two signs
questions.explanation: The two symbols look similar at speed, and the difference is exactly what you need. An added lane gives the joining vehicle somewhere to go. Merging traffic means it is arriving where you already are, so be ready to change your speed or your lane.

Continue, since the figure applies only to commercial trucks
Continue slowly, since a slow vehicle will fit where a fast one will not
Let some air out of the tyres so the van sits lower

Deflating tyres is not a safe or meaningful way to gain clearance and creates a handling hazard of its own.

Speed up so that you clear the intersection before the light changes
Ignore it unless you can actually see a red light
Move to the left lane, which is never controlled by the signal

The sign exists because you cannot see the signal yet; waiting for the red is waiting too long.
Every lane approaching the intersection is controlled by the signal.

A truck route joining the highway
questions.explanation: The sign warns you of hills where special care must be taken, and the handbook is specific about the timing: slow down before you start downhill. Once you are on the grade, your brakes are working against gravity and the whole weight of the vehicle.

Halfway down, once you can see the bottom
Only if you feel the vehicle gathering speed
At the bottom, where the road levels out

Reducing speed at the bottom is too late to help you on the grade itself.

The road surface is permanently poor along this stretch
The sign applies only to vehicles entering the work site

Only if a flagger is present at the site

The sign's status does not depend on whether a flagger happens to be on duty.

Slow or stop is signalled with the arm pointing down.

Turn quickly in front of it, since a left turn has the right-of-way

Sound your horn and proceed

questions.question: The circles in this diagram mark the No-Zone around a heavy truck. What is a No-Zone?
choices: A truck's blind spots, where the truck driver cannot see your vehicle
An area where passing a truck is illegal
The space a truck needs to come to a complete stop
A lane reserved for heavy trucks only
questions.explanation: A truck's blind spots — the No-Zone — are dangerous because truck drivers cannot see vehicles in these areas. They sit alongside, immediately behind and directly in front of the trailer, and they are far larger than a car's blind spots.
choiceExplanations: The No-Zone describes what the driver cannot see, not a legal prohibition on passing.
Stopping distance is a separate point: a loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph needs three times the distance a car does.
The No-Zone is an area of poor visibility around a truck, not a reserved lane.

Seeing part of the trailer tells you nothing about the driver's field of view from the mirrors.
Relative speed does not determine visibility; the mirror test does.

questions.question: This diagram shows an acceleration lane joining an interstate. At what speed should you be travelling as you merge?

Well below the traffic's speed, so you can see a gap open
Above the traffic's speed, so you can force your way in
Whatever speed the ramp's advisory sign showed, held all the way in
questions.explanation: As you merge, make sure you are traveling the same speed as other traffic. The acceleration lane exists to let you reach that speed, and matching it is what turns a merge into a lane change rather than an obstacle.
choiceExplanations: Entering slower than the traffic forces everyone behind you to brake and is a common cause of merge crashes.
Entering faster than the stream is no safer than entering slower; the target is the same speed.
Ramp advisory speeds apply to the curve of the ramp, not to the merge itself.

Adjust your speed to meet a gap further back in the stream
Use your turn signal before moving over
Take quick glances over your shoulder and to the side

Quick glances over your shoulder and to the side are part of checking interstate traffic while you merge.

Within 200 feet of the other vehicle
Within 100 feet of the other vehicle

questions.explanation: When meeting another vehicle at night, dim your headlight beams within 500 feet of the other vehicle. The 200-foot figure is the different case — when you are following another vehicle rather than meeting it.
choiceExplanations: 200 feet is the distance for dimming when you are following another vehicle, not meeting one.
100 feet is not a dimming distance in the handbook; it is the distance for signalling before a turn.
The duty to dim is yours regardless of what the other driver does.

Look directly at the oncoming headlights so your eyes adjust
Switch your own lights to high beam to even things out
Close your eyes briefly until the vehicle has passed
questions.explanation: Looking directly into oncoming headlights causes momentary blindness. When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, slow down, keep to the right of your traffic lane, and look well in front of your vehicle at the right edge of the road — the edge line gives you steering guidance while your eyes recover.

Retaliating with high beams blinds the other driver too and makes a head-on more likely, not less.
Closing your eyes at speed means travelling a considerable distance with no information at all.

choiceExplanations: The vehicle ahead is the one in front of you in your own lane, which may stop suddenly and without warning.
The tailgating vehicle is the one following too closely behind you.

Only on interstate ramps

questions.explanation: This situation exists at intersections, driveways, and entrances and exits to parking lots — the places where another vehicle can arrive across your path rather than along it. Learn the traffic laws and obey the signs and signals that control traffic there.
choiceExplanations: Interstate ramps are one place vehicles join a road, but driveways and parking lot exits are just as much part of this situation.

Work zones are a separate hazard; this situation applies on ordinary roads every day.

The driver ahead may be reacting to something you cannot see at all, which is why the stop can be sudden.
